steps: Make a fist with your dominant hand and stick your thumb straight up, holding it in front of your chest.
Hold your other hand in a relaxed fist beside it, about a fist-width away.
Twist your wrist sharply so the thumb flicks from pointing up to pointing across toward your other fist.
Keep your palm facing inward toward the other hand throughout the flick.
tip: “Buying” is signed with the base BUY sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you at waist level with the palm facing up.
Curve the fingers of your dominant hand into a rounded cupped shape, as if holding a coin.
Bring the cupped hand down from above and tap your fingertips once onto the open palm.
tip: “Paying” is signed with the base PAY sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Hold both hands open and flat in front of your body, fingers together.
Turn both palms to face upward, as if holding two invisible balls.
Circle both hands continuously, the left going one way and the right the other.
Keep the circles small and even, just above waist height.
Smile — play is joyful, and a stiff face reads as mechanical.
tip: Past form of “Play” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Extend the index finger of your dominant hand, folding the remaining fingers into a loose fist.
Touch your chin with the fingertip, keeping the finger pointing upward and the palm facing down.
Flick your hand forward away from your chin so the finger points ahead at chest height.
tip: “Saying” is signed with the base SAY sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.
